edges.description: The clinical expression of this endpoint node. Impaired intellectual functioning is what the class is defined by, and in the strictest members of the series it is the only feature present, so the terminal mechanism node and this phenotype stand in a direct relation with no intervening step. The remaining phenotypes in this entry - global developmental delay, speech and language delay, behavioural and autistic features, and seizures - are deliberately left unwired: they appear in some subtypes and not others, and assigning each to a mechanism node requires per-subtype evidence this pass did not gather.

evidence.reference_title: FACL4, encoding fatty acid-CoA ligase 4, is mutated in nonspecific X-linked mental retardation.
evidence.snippet: Analysis of enzymatic activity in lymphoblastoid cell lines from affected individuals of both families revealed low levels compared with normal cells, indicating that both mutations are null mutations.

evidence.reference_title: X-linked intellectual disability update 2017.
evidence.snippet: Sequence variants in 11 genes (KLF8, AFF2, SLC6A8, NDUFA1, ALG13, SRPX2, ATRX, NLGN3, FGDY, CDKL5, and NLGN4) have been found in families with IDX but in whom IDX numbers were never assigned.

evidence.reference_title: ARX, a novel Prd-class-homeobox gene highly expressed in the telencephalon, is mutated in X-linked mental retardation.
evidence.snippet: In contrast to other genes involved in XLMR, ARX expression is specific to the telencephalon and ventral thalamus.

nodes.description: Although the causal genes do not share a single pathway, their products fall repeatedly into a limited set of themes that converge on the same functional endpoint: Rho GTPase signalling to the actin cytoskeleton (PAK3), Rab-dependent synaptic vesicle recycling (GDI1), proposed roles in excitatory synapse formation and neurite outgrowth (IL1RAPL1, TSPAN7 - both inferred rather than directly demonstrated in the cited reports), tRNA anticodon-loop modification and translational fidelity (FTSJ1), fatty-acid metabolism (ACSL4), Golgi/trans-Golgi-network pH regulation and glycosylation (SLC9A7), transcriptional activation (AFF2, silenced by the FRAXE repeat expansion), and telencephalic transcriptional control (ARX). Most of these arms act on synapse formation, maintenance, and plasticity, and synaptic convergence is the field's dominant framing of the class. It is not, however, established for all of them: the tRNA-modification (FTSJ1), fatty-acid (ACSL4), Golgi-pH (SLC9A7), and transcriptional (AFF2) arms have documented molecular and cellular consequences but no cited evidence of a synaptic endpoint, so the node is deliberately named for neuronal rather than synaptic function. What is shared across every arm is that convergence happens at the level of neuronal cell biology rather than through a common molecular pathway - which is why no single pathway-directed therapy addresses the class. Enumerating the rest of the numbered series adds further themes without disturbing that conclusion: postsynaptic scaffolding at the NMDA receptor and the dendritic spine (DLG3, FRMPD4), synaptic vesicle clustering, mobility and cargo retrieval (SYN1, SYP), presynaptic terminal formation and maintenance from the Golgi (RAB39B), ubiquitin-proteasome substrate handling (MID2, KLHL15, USP27X), chromatin and transcriptional coregulation (ZNF711, ZMYM3), Arf-family guanine-nucleotide exchange (IQSEC2), serine-threonine kinase signalling (RPS6KA3) and microtubule stabilisation in developing neurons (FGF13). The ubiquitin arm is the clearest illustration that convergence here is thematic rather than directional: MID2 and KLHL15 are ubiquitin-ligase pathway components whose loss impairs degradation of specific substrates, whereas USP27X is a deubiquitinase, so the arm has no single direction and its process annotation deliberately carries no modifier. USP27X is also the one gene admitted here with essentially no characterised neuronal function, so for that arm this node records convergence without a mechanism.

evidence.reference_title: PAK3 mutation in nonsyndromic X-linked mental retardation.

evidence.reference_title: PAK3 mutation in nonsyndromic X-linked mental retardation.
evidence.snippet: Signal transduction through Rho GTPases and PAK3 may be critical for human cognitive function.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in GDI1 are responsible for X-linked non-specific mental retardation.
evidence.snippet: Rab GDP-dissociation inhibitors (GDI) are evolutionarily conserved proteins that play an essential role in the recycling of Rab GTPases required for vesicular transport through the secretory pathway.

evidence.reference_title: Defects in tRNA Anticodon Loop 2'-O-Methylation Are Implicated in Nonsyndromic X-Linked Intellectual Disability due to Mutations in FTSJ1.
evidence.snippet: tRNA modifications are crucial for efficient and accurate protein synthesis, and modification defects are frequently associated with disease.

evidence.reference_title: A recurrent missense variant in SLC9A7 causes nonsyndromic X-linked intellectual disability with alteration of Golgi acidification and aberrant glycosylation.
evidence.snippet: These data implicate a crucial role for SLC9A7 in the regulation of TGN/post-Golgi pH homeostasis and glycosylation of exported cargo, which may underlie the cellular pathophysiology and neurodevelopmental deficits associated with this particular nonsyndromic form of X-linked ID.

evidence.reference_title: Fragile XE-associated familial mental retardation protein 2 (FMR2) acts as a potent transcription activator.
evidence.snippet: Our results show that FMR2 is a potent transcription activator and that its function is conserved.

evidence.reference_title: Fragile XE-associated familial mental retardation protein 2 (FMR2) acts as a potent transcription activator.
evidence.snippet: Expansion of the FRAXE CCG repeat to a full mutation is associated with methylation and transcriptional silencing of the FMR2 gene, and as a consequence, mild-to-borderline mental retardation.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the DLG3 gene cause nonsyndromic X-linked mental retardation.
evidence.snippet: We have identified truncating mutations in the human DLG3 (neuroendocrine dlg) gene in 4 of 329 families with moderate to severe X-linked mental retardation.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the DLG3 gene cause nonsyndromic X-linked mental retardation.
evidence.snippet: DLG3 encodes synapse-associated protein 102 (SAP102), a member of the membrane-associated guanylate kinase protein family.

evidence.reference_title: 5'-UTR SNP of FGF13 causes translational defect and intellectual disability.
evidence.snippet: In both HEK293 cells and patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells, this SNP reduced the translation of FGF13, which stabilizes microtubules in developing neurons.

evidence.reference_title: 5'-UTR SNP of FGF13 causes translational defect and intellectual disability.
evidence.snippet: Furthermore, this SNP reduced the interaction between FGF13 5'-UTR and polypyrimidine-tract-binding protein 2 (PTBP2), which was required for FGF13 translation in cortical neurons.

evidence.reference_title: FRMPD4 mutations cause X-linked intellectual disability and disrupt dendritic spine morphogenesis.
evidence.snippet: Mutations include deletion of an entire coding exon, a nonsense mutation, a frame-shift mutation resulting in premature termination of translation, and a missense mutation involving a highly conserved amino acid residue neighboring FRMPD4-FERM domain.

evidence.reference_title: FRMPD4 mutations cause X-linked intellectual disability and disrupt dendritic spine morphogenesis.
evidence.snippet: FRMPD4 (FERM and PDZ Domain Containing 4) is a neural scaffolding protein that interacts with PSD-95 to positively regulate dendritic spine morphogenesis, and with mGluR1/5 and Homer to regulate mGluR1/5 signaling.

evidence.reference_title: Defects in tRNA Anticodon Loop 2'-O-Methylation Are Implicated in Nonsyndromic X-Linked Intellectual Disability due to Mutations in FTSJ1.
evidence.snippet: Additionally, tRNA(Phe) from an NSXLID patient with a novel FTSJ1-p.A26P missense allele specifically lacks Gm34 , but has normal levels of Cm32 and o2yW37 .

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in GDI1 are responsible for X-linked non-specific mental retardation.
evidence.snippet: One of the mutations caused a non-conservative substitution (L92P) which reduced binding and recycling of RAB3A, the second was a null mutation.

nodes.description: Males carry one X chromosome, so a loss-of-function allele is expressed in every cell with no second copy to buffer it. Heterozygous females are mosaic, because random X-chromosome inactivation silences one X per cell, so the mutant allele is expressed in only a subset of cells; such carriers are typically unaffected or mildly affected, and in several subtypes completely skewed X-inactivation silences the mutant X entirely. This dosage asymmetry is the mechanistic basis of the male excess observed among people with intellectual disability, and the mosaicism is the principal obstacle to studying the circuit pathophysiology in females.

evidence.reference_title: XLID-causing mutations and associated genes challenged in light of data from large-scale human exome sequencing.
evidence.snippet: Because of the unbalanced sex ratio (1.3-1.4 to 1) observed in intellectual disability (ID) and the identification of large ID-affected families showing X-linked segregation, much attention has been focused on the genetics of X-linked ID (XLID).

evidence.reference_title: Overcoming genetic and cellular complexity to study the pathophysiology of X-linked intellectual disabilities.
evidence.snippet: This mosaic expression produces substantial complexity, especially when attempting to study the already complicated neural circuits that underly behavior, thus impeding the understanding of disease-related pathophysiology and the development of therapeutics.

evidence.reference_title: FACL4, encoding fatty acid-CoA ligase 4, is mutated in nonspecific X-linked mental retardation.
evidence.snippet: All carrier females with either point mutations or genomic deletions in FACL4 showed a completely skewed X-inactivation, suggesting that the gene influences survival advantage.

evidence.reference_title: A new member of the IL-1 receptor family highly expressed in hippocampus and involved in X-linked mental retardation.
evidence.snippet: Thorough investigation of an MRX critical region in Xp22.1-21.3 enabled us to identify a new gene expressed in brain that is responsible for a non-specific form of X-linked mental retardation.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the guanine nucleotide exchange factor gene IQSEC2 cause nonsyndromic intellectual disability.
evidence.snippet: The first family identified as having a nonsyndromic intellectual disability was mapped in 1988. Here we show that a mutation of IQSEC2, encoding a guanine nucleotide exchange factor for the ADP-ribosylation factor family of small GTPases, caused this disorder.

nodes.description: The convergent synaptic lesion degrades activity-dependent plasticity in the hippocampal and cortical circuits that support learning and memory. Several causal genes are selectively or highly expressed in exactly these structures - IL1RAPL1 in the postnatal hippocampal memory system, PAK3 in postmitotic neurons of developing and postnatal cerebral cortex and hippocampus, TSPAN7 in cerebral cortex and hippocampus - which is the anatomical reason a diffuse molecular lesion produces a circumscribed cognitive phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Immunofluorescence analysis showed that PAK3 protein is highly expressed in postmitotic neurons of the developing and postnatal cerebral cortex and hippocampus.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in GDI1 are responsible for X-linked non-specific mental retardation.
evidence.snippet: Our results show that both functional and developmental alterations in the neuron may account for the severe impairment of learning abilities as a consequence of mutations in GDI1, emphasizing its critical role in development of human intellectual and learning abilities.

nodes.description: Impaired intellectual functioning and adaptive behaviour, present as the only consistent shared feature of the class. Severity spans mild to severe depending on the gene and allele. Because the class aggregates many individually rare gene-defined disorders, severity cannot be meaningfully quantified at the group level.

evidence.reference_title: A new member of the IL-1 receptor family highly expressed in hippocampus and involved in X-linked mental retardation.
evidence.snippet: Non-overlapping deletions and a nonsense mutation in this gene were identified in patients with cognitive impairment only.

evidence.reference_title: Targeted deep resequencing identifies MID2 mutation for X-linked intellectual disability with varied disease severity in a large kindred from India.
evidence.snippet: We report a novel missense mutation (c.1040G>A, p.Arg347Gln) in MID2, which encodes ubiquitin ligase E3, as the likely cause of X-linked mental retardation in a large kindred.

evidence.reference_title: Targeted deep resequencing identifies MID2 mutation for X-linked intellectual disability with varied disease severity in a large kindred from India.
evidence.snippet: When transiently expressed in HEK293T cell line, the mutation was found to abolish the function of the COS domain in the protein.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the small GTPase gene RAB39B are responsible for X-linked mental retardation associated with autism, epilepsy, and macrocephaly.
evidence.snippet: One mutation in family X (D-23) introduced a stop codon seven amino acids after the start codon (c.21C > A; p.Y7X). A second mutation, in the MRX72 family, altered the 5' splice site (c.215+1G > A) and normal splicing. Neither instance produced a protein.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the small GTPase gene RAB39B are responsible for X-linked mental retardation associated with autism, epilepsy, and macrocephaly.
evidence.snippet: We show that RAB39B, a novel RAB GTPase of unknown function, is a neuronal-specific protein that is localized to the Golgi compartment.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the RSK2(RPS6KA3) gene cause Coffin-Lowry syndrome and nonsyndromic X-linked mental retardation.
evidence.snippet: In two families, the clinical diagnosis had been nonsyndromic X-linked mental retardation.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the RSK2(RPS6KA3) gene cause Coffin-Lowry syndrome and nonsyndromic X-linked mental retardation.

evidence.reference_title: A recurrent missense variant in SLC9A7 causes nonsyndromic X-linked intellectual disability with alteration of Golgi acidification and aberrant glycosylation.
evidence.snippet: We report two unrelated families with multigenerational nonsyndromic intellectual disability (ID) segregating with a recurrent de novo missense variant (c.1543C>T:p.Leu515Phe) in the alkali cation/proton exchanger gene SLC9A7 (also commonly referred to as NHE7).

evidence.reference_title: A recurrent missense variant in SLC9A7 causes nonsyndromic X-linked intellectual disability with alteration of Golgi acidification and aberrant glycosylation.
evidence.snippet: Mass spectrometry analysis of patient sera also revealed an abnormal N-glycosylation profile for transferrin, a clinical diagnostic marker for congenital disorders of glycosylation.

evidence.reference_title: A novel SYN1 missense mutation in non-syndromic X-linked intellectual disability affects synaptic vesicle life cycle, clustering and mobility.
evidence.snippet: We identified a missense mutation (c.236 C > G; p.S79W) in the SYN1 gene coding for synapsin I in the MRX50 family, affected by non-syndromic X-linked intellectual disability.

evidence.reference_title: A novel SYN1 missense mutation in non-syndromic X-linked intellectual disability affects synaptic vesicle life cycle, clustering and mobility.
evidence.snippet: In addition, the presence of S79W Synapsin I strongly reduces the mobility of synaptic vesicles, with possible implications for the regulation of neurotransmitter release and synaptic plasticity.

evidence.snippet: The screen has discovered nine genes implicated in XLMR, including SYP, ZNF711 and CASK reported here, confirming the power of this strategy.

evidence.reference_title: X-linked intellectual disability-associated mutations in synaptophysin disrupt synaptobrevin II retrieval.
evidence.snippet: Synaptophysin is an integral synaptic vesicle (SV) protein that accounts for ∼10% of total SV protein cargo.

nodes.description: The endpoint of the class: non-progressive impairment of intellectual functioning and adaptive behaviour in a brain that is structurally normal on imaging and free of any consistently reproducible dysmorphic, metabolic, or systemic sign. This is a mis-tuned rather than a mis-built or damaged circuit, which is why brain MRI is characteristically unremarkable and why - in the absence of any distinguishing feature - molecular testing rather than clinical recognition is the only route to a specific diagnosis. The class is conventionally described as static and non-progressive, with developmental regression arguing against the diagnosis; note that none of the evidence cited on this node speaks to temporal course, so the staticity claim rests on clinical convention rather than on a source quoted here.
nodes.id: Static Cognitive Impairment Without Structural Brain Malformation

evidence.reference_title: PAK3 mutation in nonsyndromic X-linked mental retardation.
evidence.snippet: MRI analysis showed no gross defects in brain development.

evidence.reference_title: ARX, a novel Prd-class-homeobox gene highly expressed in the telencephalon, is mutated in X-linked mental retardation.
evidence.snippet: The absence of detectable brain malformations in patients suggests that ARX may have an essential role, in mature neurons, required for the development of cognitive abilities.

evidence.reference_title: Novel GDI1 mutation in a large family with nonsyndromic X-linked intellectual disability.
evidence.snippet: The present family supports the lack of additional phenotypic features in patients with GDI1 mutations, rendering a clinical diagnosis of GDI1-associated XLID impossible.

evidence.reference_title: A new gene involved in X-linked mental retardation identified by analysis of an X;2 balanced translocation.
evidence.snippet: Further investigation led to identification of TM4SF2 mutations in 2 of 33 other MRX families.

evidence.reference_title: X-exome sequencing of 405 unresolved families identifies seven novel intellectual disability genes.
evidence.snippet: In 19 families, we detected likely causative protein truncating and missense variants in 7 novel and validated XLID genes (CLCN4, CNKSR2, FRMPD4, KLHL15, LAS1L, RLIM and USP27X)

evidence.reference_title: X-exome sequencing of 405 unresolved families identifies seven novel intellectual disability genes.
evidence.snippet: Little is currently known about the functional role of the ubiquitin specific peptidase USP27X.

nodes.description: Rare germline loss-of-function, hypomorphic, repeat-expansion, or copy-number variants in any one of a large set of genes on the X chromosome remove or reduce the activity of the encoded product in the developing and mature brain. The class is clinically homogeneous but genetically heterogeneous: variants at many different loci converge on the same single clinical outcome, and each individual gene accounts for only a small fraction of cases. The X chromosome is disproportionately represented among intellectual-disability genes relative to its size.

evidence.reference_title: PAK3 mutation in nonsyndromic X-linked mental retardation.
evidence.snippet: Nonsyndromic X-linked mental retardation (MRX) syndromes are clinically homogeneous but genetically heterogeneous disorders, whose genetic bases are largely unknown.

evidence.reference_title: A new gene involved in X-linked mental retardation identified by analysis of an X;2 balanced translocation.
evidence.snippet: At least five MRX genes have been identified by positional cloning, but each accounts for only 0.5%-1.0% of MRX cases.

evidence.reference_title: X-linked intellectual disability update 2017.
evidence.snippet: The X-chromosome comprises only about 5% of the human genome but accounts for about 15% of the genes currently known to be associated with intellectual disability.

evidence.reference_title: Deleterious, protein-altering variants in the transcriptional coregulator ZMYM3 in 27 individuals with a neurodevelopmental delay phenotype.
evidence.snippet: ChIP-seq experiments on one variant, p.Arg1274Trp, indicate dramatically reduced genomic occupancy, supporting a hypomorphic effect.

evidence.reference_title: Deleterious, protein-altering variants in the transcriptional coregulator ZMYM3 in 27 individuals with a neurodevelopmental delay phenotype.
evidence.snippet: Variants in almost all individuals (n = 26) are missense, including six that recurrently affect two residues.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in two large pedigrees highlight the role of ZNF711 in X-linked intellectual disability.
evidence.snippet: Patients with mutations in ZNF711 all present with mild to moderate ID and poor speech accompanied by additional features in some patients, including autistic features and mild facial dysmorphisms, suggesting that ZNF711 mutations cause non-syndromic ID.

evidence.reference_title: A functional link between the histone demethylase PHF8 and the transcription factor ZNF711 in X-linked mental retardation.
evidence.snippet: Furthermore, PHF8 interacts with another XMLR protein, ZNF711, which binds to a subset of PHF8 target genes, including the XLMR gene JARID1C.

evidence.reference_title: A systematic, large-scale resequencing screen of X-chromosome coding exons in mental retardation.
evidence.snippet: The screen has discovered nine genes implicated in XLMR, including SYP, ZNF711 and CASK reported here, confirming the power of this strategy.
